items.title: Festive season crackdown: Maharashtra FDA seizes food stock worth ₹63.45 crore
points: According to a press note issued by the FDA, officials inspected 9,667 food establishments across Maharashtra, issued 4,603 improvement notices and initiated action to cancel 25 licences and registrations.
They also collected 8,835 food samples and seized 3,098.46 metric tonnes of food stock.

As part of the broader enforcement exercise, a Diwali special drive conducted between October 15 and November 3 saw inspections at 3,332 establishments, suspension of 326 licences and registrations, and initiation of cancellation proceedings against 15 others.
During this period, officials seized 1,886.44 metric tonnes of food stock worth ₹44.37 crore and collected 3,864 samples.

The Konkan division accounted for the highest value of seizures during the overall drive, at ₹21.17 crore, followed by Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar at ₹12.37 crore, Pune at ₹10.39 crore and Nashik at ₹10.27 crore.
In Greater Mumbai, officials inspected 1,504 establishments, suspended 142 licences and registrations, and seized food stock worth approximately ₹1.01 crore.

items.title: Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences
points: Two FIRs were registered, and four persons were arrested under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act in connection with the illegal sale of narcotic drugs.
Among the major seizures, FDA officials recovered allopathic drugs worth ₹22.03 lakh from the premises of Phoenix Medicorp in Nagpur on October 7.
In Mumbai, FDA officials seized spurious drugs identified as Empirime tablets and Cardiurex 2 ml, worth ₹1.01 lakh, from INHS Asvini in Colaba on October 29, according to the department.
In separate operations in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on October 14 and 25, officials seized 199 Nitrosun 10 tablets containing Nitrazepam.
The FDA also seized cosmetic soaps worth ₹4.05 lakh from Vedas Herbals Mahila Gruh Udyog in Baramati, Pune district, on October 14, for alleged manufacturing without a licence.
In Vasai East, officials seized raw materials, packaging materials and machinery worth ₹1.83 lakh from G.B.
The Konkan division recorded the highest number of inspections in October at 556, followed by Pune with 375 and Greater Mumbai with 322.

items.title: Brazilian builds boat from rubbish to collect more rubbish
points: A former Brazilian ocean canoeing champion has taken recycling to a floating extreme, constructing a boat from 230 discarded plastic containers so he can collect even more rubbish from the sea.

Marcos Arnhold spent two months building the unusual craft in Guaratuba, southern Brazil, using 125 two-litre plastic bottles, 105 five-litre disinfectant containers and a metal roof rack salvaged from an old Volkswagen Kombi.
The homemade vessel is destined for Guaratuba Bay and its surrounding mangroves, where Arnhold plans to collect discarded rubbish for delivery to a municipal recycling centre.
The former athlete, who won Brazil’s national ocean canoeing championship in 2002, told local newspaper JB Litoral that initial flotation and stability tests have exceeded expectations.
The vessel currently has a 6.5 hp petrol engine, although Arnhold hopes eventually to add a sail and switch to electric propulsion.
Friends donated bottles, while local sponsors helped finance the engine and trailer.

In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber.

items.title: Treasuries Soar as Tech-Stock Selloff Lures Investors to Havens
points: (Bloomberg) -- Treasuries rose as a Democratic sweep in the US midterms led to a selloff in shares of large US technology companies, stoking demand for havens.
The rally in the US government bond market on Thursday sent yields down across maturities by as much as nine basis points to the lowest levels since early September.
The yield retreat began after the US stock market opened, with the Nasdaq 100 index falling 4.75% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 8.83%.
“The fact that chip stocks are falling is an extension of the idea that there may be a pullback in the pace of capex spend,” said Anmol Sinha, fixed income investment director at The Capital Group.

items.title: Residents of disputed villages in Kotia cross Odisha border to vote in Andhra Pradesh polls
points: The Odisha government had deployed 16 platoons of police and erected three border checkpoints, restricting people’s entry and exit.
The Andhra Pradesh government had set up a polling booth for villagers of Kotia at Sariki in its State boundary.
Political parties in Odisha accused leaders from Andhra Pradesh of bribing people to get their votes.
Both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have been claiming their jurisdictional rights since 1950s.
The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages.
Odisha government had moved Supreme Court over Kotia dispute in 1968.
Koraput District Collector had filed contempt petition in the Supreme Court in October this year, alleging Andhra Pradesh violated the 2006 status quo order.
On March 30, 2006, the Supreme Court disposed of the original suit (1968), holding that it lacked jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute because of the proviso to Article 131.

items.title: JP Morgan to add Philippines and Saudi Arabia to key EM bond index over 10 months
points: JP Morgan has announced plans to include Saudi Arabia and the Philippines in its emerging market debt index starting in 2027.
The Saudi riyal-denominated sukuk and Philippine peso-denominated government bonds will be integrated over a ten-month period.
The index is expected to adjust the maximum country weight limit from 10% to 9%.
Saudi Arabia's weight will reach 2.71%, while the Philippines will have a weight of 1.64%.

items.title: AAP Leader's Delhi-Punjab Air Quality Video Sparks Fresh Face-Off With BJP
points: A political battle over air pollution between the Aam Aadmi Party and the BJP has taken a fresh turn, with an AQI-monitoring exercise by AAP leader Jarnail Singh triggering a video controversy.
What sparked it was Delhi BJP leaders questioning the date displayed on his pollution-monitoring machine.
Singh displayed a reading of around 600 for Delhi, followed by nearly 800 at Murthal, suggesting that pollution levels there were even higher than in the national capital.
At Kurukshetra, he showed a reading below 300, while the reading displayed in Mohali was around 45.
The figures were presented by Singh as evidence to counter the BJP's attempt to blame Punjab for Delhi's pollution crisis.
Issuing an open challenge to Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and BJP leaders, Singh invited them to accompany him from Delhi to Mohali and personally verify the readings at different locations.
He also challenged the Delhi Chief Minister, the Environment Minister and other BJP leaders to undertake the same journey and check the readings themselves.

items.title: The average US 30-year mortgage rate falls to 7.18% this week, its third straight decline
points: The average long-term mortgage rates in the U.S. decreased for the third consecutive week, offering some respite.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage declined to 7.18% from 7.24%, according to Freddie Mac.
Additionally, the 15-year fixed-rate mortgages saw a drop to 6.57%, slightly down from last week.
These lower rates help to alleviate the financial burden on prospective homebuyers facing increased costs.

items.title: 3 Fishermen Found Dead After Cyclone Murasu, Anger Erupts In Chennai's Kasimedu
points: The deaths of three of the nine fishermen who went missing after their boat was caught in Cyclone Murasu have triggered anger and anguish in Chennai district's Kasimedu, with grieving families questioning the government's response and demanding accountability.
The bodies of the three fishermen were found in Andhra Pradesh's Prakasam district.
The nine-member crew from Chennai's Kasimedu fishing harbour had been stranded at sea after their trawler reportedly developed a mechanical snag.
Cyclone Murasu struck as the vessel remained stranded, leaving the fishermen caught in rough seas.
Chief Minister Vijay has condoled the deaths and announced a compensation of Rs 7 lakh for each bereaved family.

But on the ground in Kasimedu, the mood is one of grief and anger, with families demanding answers on why the fishermen could not be rescued in time and what mechanisms were in place to ensure their safety.
Finance Minister Marie Wilson, who visited and consoled the affected families before travelling to Andhra Pradesh, acknowledged gaps.

items.title: 20 Years After Nano Row, Suvendu Adhikari Hopes For A Vehicle Factory In Singur
points: Twenty years ago, Singur changed the course of Bengal's politics.
After the 2006 Assembly elections, the Left Front government of then chief minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee set out to bring industry to the Hooghly farmland.
Instead, it set off a farmers' agitation that helped Mamata Banerjee drive the last nail into the coffin of Left Front rule in 2011.
Back in Bengal, on Thursday, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who heads the state's first BJP government, signalled that industry may finally return to Singur.

Adhikari said in New Town, after unveiling the state's new industrial policy, that his government had held preliminary talks with heavy commercial vehicle maker Ashok Leyland about the land once given to Tata.

items.title: 3 Labourers Killed, 9 Injured As Pick-Up Truck Overturns In Gujarat's Tapi
points: Three persons were killed and nine others injured after a pick-up truck carrying farm labourers overturned in Gujarat's Tapi district on Wednesday, police said.
The accident occurred in the morning in the Vyara taluka, they said.
The driver of the pick-up truck with 11 farm labourers on board reportedly lost control of the steering wheel, causing the vehicle to overturn, said inspector N I Barot from Kakrapar police station.

One person died on the spot, while two others succumbed to injuries during treatment, Barot said, adding that the victims have been identified as Sita Gamit (55), Arvind Rathod (55) and Gajara Gamit (70).
Nine other occupants of the vehicle, including the driver, sustained injuries and were taken to a hospital.
Police have registered a case, and further investigation is underway, the official said.

items.title: MPC Oceanic Group acquires 41% stake in Marlow Navigation

With more than 1,300 shore-based professionals across 13 countries and in excess of 16,000 crew serving on board vessels at any given time, the Marlow Group provides crew management services to shipowners and operators for more than 1,150 vessels trading…

As part of the capital increase against contributions in kind, new shares are to be issued from authorized capital at an issue price of EUR 7.00 per share.
Following completion of the capital increase, the shareholders of Marlow are expected to hold approximately 9% of MPC Oceanic Group.
It is intended to propose at the next Annual General Meeting that a representative of Marlow’s existing shareholders be appointed to the Supervisory Board of MPC Oceanic Group.

items.title: Dalian Maritime University’s Yu Jiajia to receive 2027 IMO Gender Equality Award
points: Ms Yu Jiajia, Teaching Chief Mate and instructor at Navigation College, Dalian Maritime University, has been selected to receive the 2027 IMO Gender Equality Award, following her nomination by China.

The IMO Council endorsed Ms Yu Jiajia as the recipient during its 138th session held in London (2-6 November 2026), to receive the award in May 2027, alongside celebrations for the International Day for Women in Maritime (18 May).

Ms Yu Jiajia, nominated by China, pictured here with IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez, will receive her award in May 2027 alongside celebrations for the International Day for Women in Maritime.
Pioneering a career in maritime Over the past 16 years, Ms Yu has combined her experience as a seafarer with teaching, research and advocacy to advance opportunities for women in the maritime sector.

She is the first woman under the jurisdiction of China’s Liaoning Maritime Safety Administration to obtain a Certificate of Competency for serving on ships engaged on Unlimited Navigation Areas, qualifying her to work on ships operating worldwide.

items.title: Marine Impact Lab programme brings policy, propulsion and finance into focus at Metstrade
points: How marine businesses respond to regulation, adopt alternative propulsion and fund sustainability projects will be in focus at the Marine Impact Lab at Metstrade on 16 November.
Joining the programme to tackle these questions are ICOMIA’s Patrick Hemp, ePropulsion’s Yann Herriot and Rick Wall of RAI Amsterdam and OCEANOVATION.

They join previously announced contributors including sustainability specialist Dr Susie Tomson, Veda Pretorius of IFBSO and the African Boating Conference, Composite Recycling’s Dr Pascal Gallo, nlcomp’s Alessandro Stagni and Gurit’s Paolo Manganelli.

Taking place on Monday 16 November at RAI Amsterdam, the Lab combines two practical workshops with eight expert-led Topic Tables, giving participants space to work through the decisions facing their businesses.
In “Sustainable Design Principles”, led by Marine Futures, participants will learn how lifecycle assessment can guide lower-impact boat design, then apply those principles in a team challenge.
In partnership with DAME and Yachting Ventures, marine industry innovators and start-ups will learn how to embed sustainability into their value proposition and future-proof their businesses.

items.title: Women4Oceans launches a global platform connecting women across the ocean sector
points: Evolving from its original directory, Women4Oceans helps women connect and share their work, while making it easier for organisations, media and event organisers to find women with the expertise they need.

In late September 2026, The Ocean and Us launched the newly evolved Women4Oceans platform, expanding its original directory into a global space where women working across the ocean sector can connect, exchange knowledge and discover opportunities.
The platform has already welcomed more than 200 members across over 50 countries, reflecting the diversity and global reach of the ocean community.
Founded by ocean advocate Farah Obaidullah in 2016, Women4Oceans began as a Facebook group before growing into a global network and an online directory.
Women4Oceans seeks to change that”, says Farah Obaidullah, founder of Women4Oceans and The Ocean and Us.

items.title: U.S. Initial Jobless Claims Fall, Signaling Strength in Labor Market
points: In a noteworthy development for the U.S. labor market, the latest data on initial jobless claims has shown a decline, reflecting a robust employment environment.
The number of individuals filing for unemployment insurance for the first time dropped to 189,000, underscoring a stronger-than-expected job market performance.
This figure comes in below the forecasted 197,000 claims, indicating a positive surprise for the U.S. economy.
The previous week’s claims stood at 195,000, highlighting a consistent downward trend.
This reduction in jobless claims suggests that the labor market is not only stable but potentially gaining momentum, which could have broader implications for economic growth and monetary policy.
The initial jobless claims report, while a routine release, holds significant weight as it provides the earliest glimpse into the health of the labor market.

Market participants and policymakers alike will be closely watching these developments, as sustained improvements in the labor market could influence future decisions by the Federal Reserve regarding interest rates and other monetary policies.
